# Plugin Backend

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/plugins/backend/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

The backend entry (`backend.entry` in `plugin.json`) is an ES module. The panel
imports it and calls the hooks on the default export.

```javascript
export default {
  async onLoad(ctx) {},
  async onEnable(ctx) {},
  async onDisable(ctx) {},
  async onUnload(ctx) {},
};
```

| Hook | When | Register routes? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onLoad` | The plugin is activated: an admin enabled it, or the panel started with it already enabled and its consent is current. | Yes. This is the only hook that may register routes. |
| `onEnable` | An admin enables it, or the panel starts with it already enabled | No. Register tasks, WebSocket handlers, and event listeners here. |
| `onDisable` | An admin disables it | No. The host stops tasks and drops WebSocket handlers. Event listeners stay until unload. |
| `onUnload` | Plugin removed from the registry (uninstall, or a reload) | No. Last chance to release anything you opened yourself. Event listeners come off here. |

Nothing executes before an accepted safety disclaimer. Discovery only reads
`plugin.json`: the backend module is not imported and `onLoad` does not run
until an admin enables the plugin. An update that changes the version or the
declared permissions drops back to that state, so the new code stays inert
until it is accepted again.

Routes stay mounted after disable and return `503` until the next enable.
Tasks do not survive a restart; `onEnable` must register them again.

## Context

Every hook receives the same context.

| Member | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest` | The validated manifest. |
| `originalConfig` | The `config` block exactly as declared in `plugin.json`, before admin values were merged in. |
| `installId` | Stable, opaque identity for this panel install. See [Plugin licensing](/api/plugins/licensing/). |
| `logger` | Pino logger, child-bound to the plugin name. |
| `wsGateway` | Scoped WebSocket host. `sendToAgent` needs `console.write` or `server.write`; `broadcastToAuthenticated` and `sendToClient` are ungated. Host internals (client and agent maps) are not reachable. |
| `db` | Scoped database. See [Data](/api/plugins/data/). |
| `registerRoute(options)` | Mount a route under `/api/plugins/<name>`. |
| `registerMiddleware(handler, { scope })` | `scope` is `'global'` (default) or `'route'`. |
| `requirePermission(...tokens)` | Returns a `preHandler` that 403s unless the **caller** holds a token. |
| `hasPermission(request, ...tokens)` | Soft check. `*` on the user satisfies it. |
| `getUserId(request)` | `request.user.userId` (falling back to `.id`), or `null`. |
| `getConfig(key)` / `setConfig(key, value)` | Plugin config values. See [Data](/api/plugins/data/). |
| `getStorage` / `setStorage` / `deleteStorage`, `collection(name)` | Plugin-scoped key-value store and document collections. See [Data](/api/plugins/data/). |
| `scheduleTask(cron, handler)` | Scheduled work. Host clears it on disable. |
| `on(event, handler)` / `emit(event, data)` | Event bus shared by plugins and the host. |
| `emitTyped(event, data)` | Same as `emit`, plus a warning when a declared payload field is missing or the event is undeclared. It never rejects the emit. |
| `onWebSocketMessage(type, handler)` | Handle `plugin:<name>:<type>`. |
| `sendWebSocketMessage(target, message)` | `target` is a client id, or `'*'` to broadcast. |
| `exposeApi(name, handler)` / `callPluginApi(plugin, api, params)` | Plugin-to-plugin calls. Caller needs `plugin.rpc`. |
| `fileTunnel` | Present on a normal panel. File operations on a node's server directory, gated per operation. |
| `auth` | Present on a normal panel. Sign-in bridge. See [Sign-in](/api/plugins/auth/). |
| `getDeclaredEvents()` | The manifest `events` map. |

## Routes

```javascript
ctx.registerRoute({
  method: 'GET',
  url: '/hello',
  preHandler: ctx.requirePermission('server.read'),
  handler: async (request) => {
    return { success: true, userId: ctx.getUserId(request) };
  },
});
```

`url: '/hello'` becomes `GET /api/plugins/my-plugin/hello`. The SDK builder
produces the same objects:

```typescript
import { defineRoutes } from '@catalyst/plugin-sdk';

const routes = defineRoutes((router) => {
  router
    .get('/hello', async () => ({ success: true }))
    .post('/echo', async (request) => ({ success: true, echoed: request.body }))
    .put('/items/:id', async () => ({ success: true }));
});
for (const route of routes) ctx.registerRoute(route);
```

Auth modes, set on `config.auth`:

| Mode | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `required` (default) | No session or [API key](/api/authentication/) → 401. `request.user` is set. |
| `optional` | A valid session sets `request.user`; anonymous callers still reach the handler. |
| `public` | Session is never required. Use for OAuth redirects and callbacks. |

`optional` and `public` only stick when the plugin holds a live `routes.public`
grant. Without it the route is downgraded to `required` (a warning is logged),
and revoking the grant re-secures the route on the next request.

### Caller permissions on a route

`config.requiredPermissions` makes the host check the **caller** before your
handler runs, so authorization does not depend on your code remembering it:

```javascript
ctx.registerRoute({
  method: 'POST',
  url: '/settings',
  config: { requiredPermissions: ['admin.write'] },
  handler: async (request) => ({ success: true }),
});
```

- The caller must hold at least one listed token (OR), evaluated with `hasGrant`
  semantics against the caller's panel permissions — see
  [the permission table](/api/plugins/manifest/#permissions-you-can-declare).
- The check runs after authentication and before any plugin hook. A caller who
  fails it gets `403` with `code: "PLUGIN_ROUTE_FORBIDDEN"`.
- `public` routes skip the check entirely. On an `optional` route an
  anonymous caller has no permissions, so it fails the check and gets `403`.
- Tokens are trimmed, deduped, shape-validated, and capped at 16. A token that
  fails the shape check (for example a scoped `server.read:srv_1`) is dropped
  and logged as a warning, because a dropped token makes the route *less*
  restricted than you asked for.
- Declaring a token the plugin itself has not been granted is also logged. The
  route still registers, but it will deny every caller until the grant exists.
- Omitting the list keeps the default: any authenticated caller passes.

`requirePermission` checks the **user**, not the plugin. The scoped database
checks the **plugin grant**. You want both: a route that reads servers should
use `preHandler: ctx.requirePermission('server.read')` and `ctx.db.servers`,
so a normal user cannot call it and a revoked plugin cannot read. A token you
declare in the manifest's `userPermissions` works here too — an admin grants it
to a role, and `ctx.requirePermission('tickets.view')` then passes for those
users. See [Data & permissions](/api/plugins/data/#two-permission-namespaces).

Return `{ success: true, ... }` and use `reply.status(code).send(...)` for
errors. The frontend client in `@catalyst/plugin-sdk/frontend` treats a body
with `success` as the whole response.

## Tasks

`scheduleTask` takes a five-field cron expression. The panel does not call
this a task in the server-owner sense — a [task](/users/tasks/) is a scheduled
action on one server. This is in-process scheduled work, and it dies when the
plugin is disabled or the process restarts.

```javascript
async onEnable(ctx) {
  if (ctx.getConfig('cronEnabled') !== false) {
    ctx.scheduleTask('*/5 * * * *', async () => {
      const n = (await ctx.getStorage('runs')) || 0;
      await ctx.setStorage('runs', n + 1);
    });
  }
}
```

## Events

The host emits these from server power actions (start, stop, restart, kill).
A node agent reporting a status change on its own does not emit them.

| Event | When | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server:status-changed` | A power action changes status | `{ serverId, status, action, timestamp }` |
| `server:started` | Status becomes `starting` — a start or restart was accepted | same |
| `server:stopped` | Status becomes `stopping` or `stopped` | same |

`server:started` fires on start-accept with `status: 'starting'` — one event per
accepted start or restart. The host also emits it for a `running` status, but no
caller sends that today, so filter on `status` rather than counting firings. For
confirmed-up, wait for the panel's `server_state_update` frame or poll
`GET /api/servers/:id`.

Your own events are plain strings. Prefix them with the plugin name
(`my-plugin:ready`) so another plugin can subscribe without colliding.
Declare them in the manifest `events` block.

## WebSocket

```javascript
ctx.onWebSocketMessage('ping', async (data, clientId) => {
  if (clientId) {
    ctx.sendWebSocketMessage(clientId, { type: 'pong', echo: data });
  }
});
```

The host prefixes the type: clients send and receive
`plugin:my-plugin:ping`. `sendWebSocketMessage('*', message)` broadcasts.
Register handlers in `onEnable`; disable removes them.

To push a frame into a node's agent console, use
`ctx.wsGateway.sendToAgent(nodeId, message)`. It throws when the grant is gone
and re-reads it on every call, so a revocation applies without a reload.

## Plugin-to-plugin calls

```javascript
// ticketing-plugin
ctx.exposeApi('getOpenCount', async ({ serverId }) => {
  return ctx.collection('tickets').count({ serverId, status: 'open' });
});

// caller — manifest must include "plugin.rpc"
const count = await ctx.callPluginApi('ticketing-plugin', 'getOpenCount', {
  serverId,
});
```

The grant is checked on every call. Calls time out at 10 seconds. After 5
consecutive failures the host opens a circuit for about 30 seconds; one probe
is then allowed through. Handle that error instead of retrying in a loop.

## File tunnel

`ctx.fileTunnel.queueRequest` runs a file operation on a server's directory
through the node agent. It is how
[fastdl-sync](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/fastdl-sync)
copies content between servers on the same node.

```javascript
const result = await ctx.fileTunnel.queueRequest(
  nodeId,        // node the server runs on
  'list',        // see the operation table below
  serverUuid,    // server UUID, not the panel id
  '/cstrike',    // path inside the server directory
  {},            // operation-specific data
);
if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.error);
```

Every operation is classified and gated on the plugin's live grants:

| Operation | Class | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list`, `download`, `archive-contents` | read | `files.read`, `files.write`, `server.read`, or `server.write` |
| `upload`, `write`, `create`, `delete`, `rename`, `permissions`, `compress`, `decompress`, `install-url` | write | `files.write` or `server.write` |
| anything else | unknown | denied |

`install-url` makes the node fetch a URL into the server directory, so it
counts as a write. An operation the classifier does not know fails closed — a
plugin cannot reach a new agent capability before the host gate learns about
it. Grants are re-read on every call, so a revocation applies to the next
operation without a reload; the call throws `Permission denied: …` and the
host logs a warning.

`download` returns bytes on `result.body`. `upload` takes those bytes as the
last argument. Requests are capped per node and time out (60 seconds, longer
for large uploads). The method is absent only when the host did not provide a
tunnel — check `ctx.fileTunnel` before calling it.

The tunnel does not filter by server ownership. A plugin that holds a node id
and a server UUID can read that server's files. Declare `files.read` /
`files.write` so the consent dialog and the gate agree, and check
`requirePermission` plus `ctx.db.servers` before you touch a path.

## Middleware

`registerMiddleware(handler, { scope })` takes a Fastify-shaped
`(request, reply, done)` handler; pass an error to `done(err)`. Register it from
`onEnable` if it should only run while enabled.

Only the `'global'` scope runs: the loader collects `scope: 'global'` middleware
and runs it before the enabled check on every route of the plugin.
`scope: 'route'` is accepted and stored but never applied, so leave it alone.

## Request limits

Every plugin route is wrapped in a gate with three limits:

| Limit | Value today | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request timeout | 30 s | The handler is abandoned and the caller gets `504`. |
| Concurrent requests | 10 per plugin | Further calls get `503` until one finishes. |
| Heap pressure | 1024 MB process-wide | Warn-only: the process heap is compared to this threshold and a throttle-logged warning is emitted. It never rejects a request, and it is not per-plugin usage. |

These are the built-in defaults and they are what runs: the loader reads
`config.requestTimeoutMs`, `config.maxConcurrentRequests`, and
`config.memoryLimitMb` from a point where `manifest.config` already holds
runtime *values*, not the field schemas, so a `config` entry of the same name
does not change them. Treat the numbers above as fixed. The heap threshold is
the only one with a working override: the `PLUGIN_PROCESS_HEAP_LIMIT_MB`
environment variable on the backend.

## Testing without a panel

`@catalyst/plugin-sdk/testing` exports `createTestPlugin` (load/enable/disable/
unload a plugin against a mock context) and `createMockContext` (records
`registerRoute` calls, keeps collections in memory with `$set`, `$unset`,
`$inc`, `$push`, `$pull` and dotted paths). `createMockLicense` covers the
licensing flow. See [Create a plugin](/api/plugins/creating/#5-develop-against-the-sdk).

## Related

- [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) — the fields these hooks read
- [Plugin Data & Permissions](/api/plugins/data/) — config, storage, scoped database
- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the panel REST API these routes sit beside

# Plugin Frontend

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/plugins/frontend/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

`frontend.entry` in `plugin.json` points at an ES module. The panel loads it
two ways:

1. **Compiled in.** A checkout of `catalyst-plugins` is bundled with the panel
   frontend. The module shares the panel's React, so hooks work. This is how
   official plugins render.
2. **Runtime bundle.** A marketplace install with no compiled copy is loaded
   from `/plugins-assets/<name>/frontend.mjs`. That file is one self-contained
   ESM bundle. It has its own React copy, and **hooks throw**. Use it for
   static UI, or ship the plugin in the repository so it is compiled in.

The loader only reads the module when the plugin is enabled and the manifest
has a `frontend` block.

## Definition

Default-export the object returned by `createFrontendPlugin`:

```typescript
import { createFrontendPlugin, createPluginApi } from '@catalyst/plugin-sdk/frontend';
import { AdminTab, ServerTab } from './components';

const api = createPluginApi('my-plugin');

export default createFrontendPlugin({
  manifest: {
    name: 'my-plugin',
    version: '1.0.0',
    displayName: 'My Plugin',
    description: 'What this UI does',
    author: 'Your Name',
  },
  tabs: [
    {
      id: 'my-plugin-admin',
      label: 'My Plugin',
      icon: 'Puzzle',
      component: AdminTab,
      location: 'admin',
      order: 100,
      requiredPermissions: ['admin.read'],
    },
    {
      id: 'my-plugin-server',
      label: 'My Plugin',
      icon: 'Zap',
      component: ServerTab,
      location: 'server',
      order: 100,
      requiredPermissions: ['server.read'],
    },
  ],
  routes: [
    { path: '/my-plugin', component: AdminTab, requiredPermissions: ['server.read'] },
  ],
  components: [
    {
      slot: 'dashboard-widgets',
      component: MyWidget,
      order: 50,
      requiredPermissions: ['server.read'],
    },
  ],
  onMount: () => {},
  onUnmount: () => {},
});
```

`onMount` runs when the module is first imported. `onUnmount` runs when a
hot reload replaces it. Neither runs per page navigation.

If the default export has no `manifest` object, the loader falls back to
legacy named exports: `AdminTab`, `ServerTab`, `UserPage`, `slots`, and
`registerSlots()`. New plugins should use the definition above. Official
plugins all do.

## Tabs

| Property | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | yes | Unique among your tabs. |
| `label` | yes | Sidebar label. |
| `component` | yes | React component. |
| `location` | yes | `'admin'` or `'server'`. |
| `icon` | no | Accepted for compatibility, but the panel does not render it: admin and server tabs always draw a fixed plug icon. |
| `order` | no | Lower comes first. Default 50. |
| `requiredPermissions` | no | Hidden unless the signed-in user holds them. Default is `admin.read` for admin tabs and `server.read` for server tabs. |
| `templateFilter` | no | Server tabs only. Hides the tab unless the server matches. |

A server-tab component receives `{ serverId: string }`.

`templateFilter` limits a server tab to matching servers. While the server
record is still loading, a filtered tab stays hidden.

```typescript
templateFilter: {
  namePattern: 'counter-strike',          // case-insensitive regex against the template name
  env: { SRCDS_APPID: '10' },              // every entry must match the server environment, case-insensitive
}
```

[cs16-admin](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/cs16-admin)
uses this so its tab only appears on Counter-Strike 1.6 servers.

## Pages

`routes[].path` is an app path (`/my-plugin`). The panel renders `component`
when the location matches. There is no router nesting; keep paths to a single
segment unless you have confirmed the panel route that mounts them.

## Slots

`components[].slot` injects a component where the panel already mounts a slot.
Only these names render today:

| Slot | Rendered in |
| --- | --- |
| `dashboard-widgets` | Dashboard, below the activity list |
| `profile-connections` | Profile page, below the linked-accounts card |
| `server-header-stats` | Server detail header, between DISK and NETWORK |

| Property | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slot` | yes | Slot name from the table above. |
| `component` | yes | React component. |
| `order` | no | Lower comes first. Default 50. |
| `requiredPermissions` | no | Hidden unless the signed-in user holds one of them. Omit to show it to everyone who can reach the surface. |

A `server-header-stats` component receives
`{ serverId, serverStatus, backupAllocationMb }`. `serverStatus` is the
server's stored status, and the component renders even when the metrics stream
is down — it is not gated on a live reading. The slot mounts only once the
server record has loaded.

[discord-oauth](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/discord-oauth)
uses `profile-connections` for its link/unlink card. Any other slot name is
accepted, stored, and never mounted — `sidebar-bottom` is one of those.

### Who sees your UI

Every signed-in user loads the plugin store, so visibility is yours to decide:

- **No `requiredPermissions`** — the component, tab or page renders for anyone
  who can reach the surface it is mounted on.
- **Built-in permissions** — the host evaluates them for the viewer. On a
  server surface that includes server-scoped grants, so an owner or a subuser
  holding `backup.read` on that server sees the UI even though they hold no
  panel-wide admin permission. `*`, `admin.read` and `admin.write` keep their
  usual widening behaviour.
- **Your own permissions** — declare them in `plugin.json` (see
  [Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/)) and an admin can grant them to a role.
  The role editor lists them under **Plugins**. Tokens you do not declare
  still work in `requiredPermissions`, but nobody can be granted them, so only
  `*` holders would see that UI.

Admins keep the full plugin inventory (consent state, licensing, capability
counts, config). Everyone else gets a reduced list — name, version, display
name, description and author of the **enabled** plugins that ship a frontend —
purely so the panel can mount the UI each plugin targets. That does tell a
signed-in user which plugins are installed; a plugin's bundle
(`/plugins-assets/...`) is reachable for the same reason. Disabled plugins,
backend-only plugins and sourcemaps stay admin-only, and the per-plugin detail
and frontend-manifest endpoints are unchanged.

## Calling your backend

`createPluginApi` prefixes `/api/plugins/<name>/` and sends cookies.

```typescript
const api = createPluginApi('my-plugin');

const hello = await api.get<{ message: string }>('hello');
const created = await api.post('items', { name: 'map' });
await api.put('items/1', { name: 'map2' });
await api.patch('items/1', { name: 'map3' });
await api.del('items/1'); // api.delete is the same call
```

A response is `{ success, data?, error? }`. HTTP failures come back as
`{ success: false, error }` rather than throwing. Paths are relative to the
plugin prefix — pass `'hello'`, not `'/api/plugins/my-plugin/hello'`.

Wrap tab trees in `PluginErrorBoundary` from the same module so a render
error in your component does not blank the page around it:

```typescript
import { PluginErrorBoundary } from '@catalyst/plugin-sdk/frontend';

export function AdminTab() {
  return (
    <PluginErrorBoundary pluginName="my-plugin">
      {/* tab body */}
    </PluginErrorBoundary>
  );
}
```

## The runtime bundle

Marketplace UI that is not compiled into the panel needs `frontend/frontend.mjs`
inside the package. `frontend/frontend.mjs` is generated, not committed: any
plugin with a `vite.config.mts` (ai-assistant, cs16-admin, discord-oauth,
fastdl-sync, licensed-example, oidc-sso) gets one from
[`scripts/build-bundles.mjs`](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/blob/main/scripts/build-bundles.mjs)
before packing. egg-explorer, example-plugin, and ticketing-plugin have no Vite
config, so their UI only renders when the panel compiled it in.

Build with Vite in library mode:

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import path from 'path';

const repoRoot = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  define: { 'process.env.NODE_ENV': '"production"' },
  resolve: {
    alias: [
      // @catalyst/plugin-sdk is not on npm: the SDK's frontend entry is
      // vendored in catalyst-plugins/sdk-frontend and aliased here.
      {
        find: '@catalyst/plugin-sdk/frontend',
        replacement: path.resolve(repoRoot, 'sdk-frontend/index.ts'),
      },
    ],
  },
  build: {
    lib: {
      entry: 'frontend/index.ts',
      formats: ['es'],
      fileName: () => 'frontend.mjs',
    },
    outDir: 'dist',
    emptyOutDir: true,
    rollupOptions: { output: { inlineDynamicImports: true } },
  },
});
```

Then move `dist/frontend.mjs` to `frontend/frontend.mjs` before packing. The
bundle must inline every dependency, including React, and must not contain a
bare import. `scripts/build-bundles.mjs` does both steps for every plugin that
has a `vite.config.mts`.

**Caution**
`frontend.mjs` cannot call React hooks. `useState`, `useEffect`, and context
hooks throw because the bundle's React is not the panel's React. Interactive
UI belongs in a plugin the panel compiles, which is the official-repository
path.

Backend-only plugins omit `frontend` entirely.

## Related

- [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) — `userPermissions` and the fields the frontend reads
- [Plugin Backend](/api/plugins/backend/) — the routes the UI calls
- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the panel REST API `createPluginApi` sits beside

---

# Plugin Data & Permissions

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/plugins/data/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

A plugin has three stores, and a narrow window onto panel data. Use the
stores for your own records. Use `context.db` only to read servers and users
you were granted.

## Config

`getConfig(key)` returns the value an admin saved, or the `default` from
`plugin.json`. It never returns the schema object.

```javascript
const greeting = ctx.getConfig('greeting') ?? 'Hello';
const enabled = ctx.getConfig('cronEnabled'); // boolean, not { type, default }
await ctx.setConfig('greeting', 'Hi');
```

`setConfig` persists the value on the plugin row. The admin UI keeps rendering
the schema. Keys must match the manifest config map; see
[Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/).

Put secrets in a `password` field. Do not hard-code them.

## Key-value storage

`getStorage` / `setStorage` / `deleteStorage` are a JSON blob per key, scoped
to the plugin. Missing keys return `null`.

```javascript
const first = await ctx.getStorage('initialized');
if (!first) {
  await ctx.setStorage('initialized', true);
  await ctx.setStorage('installDate', new Date().toISOString());
}
await ctx.deleteStorage('installDate');
```

Fine for flags and small counters. Not fine for a list that grows without a
bound — use a collection.

## Collections

```javascript
const tickets = ctx.collection('tickets');

const created = await tickets.insert({
  serverId: 'srv_123',
  subject: 'Server will not start',
  status: 'open',
});

const open = await tickets.find(
  { serverId: 'srv_123', status: 'open' },
  { sort: { createdAt: -1 }, limit: 50, skip: 0 },
);

await tickets.update({ _id: created._id }, { $set: { status: 'resolved' } });
await tickets.delete({ _id: created._id });
const n = await tickets.count({ status: 'open' });
```

`insert` adds `_id`, `_createdAt`, and `_updatedAt`. Filters support dotted
paths (`sla.resolutionBreached`) and these operators: `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`,
`$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$in`, `$nin`, `$exists`, `$regex`, `$or`, `$and`.

Updates accept `$set`, `$unset`, `$inc`, `$push`, and `$pull`. `$set` keys
may be dotted.

Typed wrapper:

```typescript
import { createTypedCollection } from '@catalyst/plugin-sdk/storage';

interface Ticket {
  _id?: string;
  serverId: string;
  subject: string;
  status: 'open' | 'resolved';
}

const tickets = createTypedCollection<Ticket>('tickets', ctx.collection('tickets'));
```

### Which engine

| `storageEngine` | Behavior | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omitted or `"legacy"` | One JSON array per collection, loaded fully for every query | Under about 1,000 documents |
| `"dedicated"` | One database row per document | Anything you would paginate |

[ticketing-plugin](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/ticketing-plugin)
and
[discord-oauth](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/discord-oauth)
set `"storageEngine": "dedicated"`. The collection API is the same either way.
Pick `dedicated` unless you know the collection stays small.

There is no row-level security. `server.read` returns every server on the
panel, not the ones the calling user owns. Filter in your handler after
`requirePermission`, and do not assume the database did it for you.

## Reading panel data

`ctx.db.servers` requires a live `server.read` grant. `ctx.db.users` requires
`user.read`. Any other table throws. The `.write` tokens grant no table access
on their own, so a plugin that updates servers declares `server.read` **and**
`server.write`. `credentials`, API keys, and audit logs are blocked even for
`*`-adjacent custom tokens; `*` itself only adds `servers` and `users`.

Reads always project a fixed field set. Requesting other fields drops them.

Server fields: `id`, `name`, `uuid`, `description`, `status`, `createdAt`,
`updatedAt`, `nodeId`, `ownerId`, `templateId`, `locationId`,
`allocatedMemoryMb`, `allocatedCpuCores`, `allocatedDiskMb`, `allocatedSwapMb`,
`containerId`, `containerName`, `networkMode`, `primaryPort`, `primaryIp`,
`environment`, `startupCommand`, `suspendedAt`, `suspensionReason`.

User fields: `id`, `username`, `email`, `name`, `image`, `banned`,
`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `role`.

```javascript
const servers = await ctx.db.servers.findMany({
  select: { id: true, name: true, status: true, uuid: true, nodeId: true },
  orderBy: { name: 'asc' },
  take: 25,
});
const one = await ctx.db.servers.findUnique({ where: { id } });
const count = await ctx.db.servers.count();
```

`update` signatures are `(id, data)`, not Prisma's `{ where, data }`.

```javascript
await ctx.db.servers.update(id, { status: 'suspended' });
```

`server.write` keeps `status` and discards every other field. If nothing
whitelisted remains, the call throws. `user.write` keeps nothing — the
whitelist is empty on purpose, so a plugin cannot write `roleIds` and grant
itself a role. Role changes go through the auth bridge (`roles.assign`), which
is audited. See [Sign-in plugins](/api/plugins/auth/).

Grants are re-read on every call. An admin revoking `server.read` makes the
next `findMany` throw. You do not need to reload the plugin.

## What enabling checks

Enabling (`POST /api/plugins/:name/enable`) requires a current safety
acceptance when any of these is true:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `never_accepted` | No acceptance on record |
| `plugin_updated` | `version` changed since acceptance |
| `permissions_grew` | The manifest declares a permission the accepted snapshot does not cover |
| `disclaimer_updated` | The panel disclaimer text version changed |

The enable body is `{ "enabled": true, "safety": { "disclaimerVersion": "1" } }`.
When consent is missing the panel responds `409` with `code:
"SAFETY_CONSENT_REQUIRED"` and the permission list the dialog renders. The
panel UI sends this; call it yourself only if you are driving enable through
the API.

Disabling never requires consent. Uninstall (`POST /api/plugins/:name/uninstall`)
accepts `{ "purgeData": true }` to also delete stored keys, collections, and
the plugin row. Omit `purgeData` to remove the code and leave the data.

Admins can revoke individual declared permissions after enable
(`PUT /api/plugins/:name/permissions` with `{ "granted": ["server.read"] }`).
The list must be a subset of the manifest. Revocation is the lever for data
access; it does not unload your routes.

## Two permission namespaces

`permissions` in `plugin.json` is the plugin's own capability list — what an
admin grants to *the plugin* so it can call host APIs. `userPermissions` is the
other direction: tokens you invent for *panel users*, which an admin grants to
a role.

```json
"userPermissions": [
  { "id": "tickets.view", "label": "View the ticket queue" }
]
```

- The role editor lists them under **Plugins**, and only while your plugin is
  enabled. Ids that are also built-in permissions are left to the built-in
  categories, so use the built-in token directly in that case.
- A role grant reaches your backend routes: `ctx.requirePermission('tickets.view')`
  succeeds for a user holding that token, exactly like a built-in one.
- `PUT /api/plugins/:name/permissions` does not touch them. It replaces the
  plugin's own grants, and rejects tokens that are not in `permissions`.

See [Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) for the declaration rules and
[Plugin Frontend](/api/plugins/frontend/) for gating tabs, pages and slots on
the same ids.

## Related

- [Plugin Backend](/api/plugins/backend/) — where `ctx.db` and storage are used
- [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) — config fields, declared permissions, and `userPermissions`
- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the panel API this data mirrors

---

# Sign-in Plugins

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/plugins/auth/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

A sign-in plugin puts a button on the login page and, after the external
provider redirects back, creates a normal panel session. Password login,
[API keys](/api/authentication/), and two-factor settings are unchanged. The
official examples are
[discord-oauth](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/discord-oauth)
and
[oidc-sso](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/oidc-sso).

## Prerequisites

Declare all four of these, or the pieces that depend on them silently do less:

| Permission | Unlocks |
| --- | --- |
| `routes.public` | `authorize` and `callback` routes that have no panel session yet |
| `auth.users` | `ctx.auth.findUser`, `ctx.auth.createUser` |
| `auth.sessions` | `ctx.auth.createSession` |
| `roles.assign` | Role listing and assignment, if you mirror groups |

`auth.sessions` and `roles.assign` are marked critical in the consent dialog.
Say what you use them for in `permissionDescriptions`.

## 1. Declare the button

```json
"authProviders": [
  { "id": "discord", "label": "Discord", "authorizePath": "authorize" }
]
```

While the plugin is **enabled**, each entry becomes a
"Continue with `{label}`" button on the login page (`auth` namespace key
`sso.continueWithProvider`). The button links to
`/api/plugins/<name>/<authorizePath>`. `authorizePath` defaults to
`authorize`. `id` is 1–32 characters, `label` is 1–64, and you may declare at
most 8 providers. Enable the plugin from **Admin → Extensions → Plugins** and
the buttons appear — there is no separate sign-in settings screen.

The list is public (`GET /api/auth/oauth-providers`) so the login page can
render it before anyone has a session. It returns
`{ success: true, providers: [{ plugin, id, label, authorizeUrl }] }`, and only
enabled plugins are listed because a disabled plugin's authorize route
answers `503`.

## 2. Register public routes

```javascript
async onLoad(ctx) {
  ctx.registerRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    url: '/authorize',
    config: { auth: 'optional' },
    handler: async (request, reply) => {
      const userId = ctx.getUserId(request); // set when an already-signed-in user is linking
      // redirect to the provider
      return reply.redirect(authorizeUrl);
    },
  });

  ctx.registerRoute({
    method: 'GET',
    url: '/callback',
    config: { auth: 'public' },
    handler: async (request, reply) => {
      // exchange the code, then find or create the user, then:
      await ctx.auth.createSession(user.id, {
        reply,
        rememberMe: true,
        ipAddress: request.ip,
        userAgent: request.headers['user-agent'],
      });
      return reply.redirect('/');
    },
  });
}
```

`optional` on `authorize` lets a signed-in user start a link flow and an
anonymous user start a login flow. `public` on `callback` is required because
the provider redirects a browser that may have no panel cookie yet.

Both modes are downgraded to `required` unless `routes.public` is currently
granted — see [Plugin Backend](/api/plugins/backend/#routes) for the full
auth-mode rules and what happens when a grant is revoked.

## 3. Use the auth bridge

`ctx.auth` is present on a normal panel. Every method checks the live grant
and throws if it is missing.

```javascript
const existing = await ctx.auth.findUser({ email });          // or { userId } or { username }
// PluginAuthUser: { id, email, username, name, image, emailVerified, banned, lockedUntil }

const created = await ctx.auth.createUser({
  email,
  username,          // 1–32 of [a-zA-Z0-9._-]
  name,
  emailVerified: true,
  image: null,
});

const session = await ctx.auth.createSession(created.id, { reply, rememberMe: true });
// session is { token, expiresAt }; passing reply sets the session cookie
```

`createUser` creates an account with no password. Those users come back
through your plugin. Duplicate email or username throws.

`createSession` writes a real session cookie, the same one password login
sets. `rememberMe` defaults to `true`; pass `rememberMe: false` for a
browser-session cookie. Refuse banned users and users with a `lockedUntil` in
the future before you call it.

On failure, redirect to:

```text
/login?oauthError=<code>&providerLabel=<label>
```

The login page shows a failure notice for that query shape. Use a short
stable `oauthError` code (`access_denied`, `email_unverified`), not a sentence.

## 4. Mirror roles

Role changes are audited. Pass `reason` so the audit log says why.

```javascript
const roles = await ctx.auth.listRoles();                 // { id, name, description }[]
const mine = await ctx.auth.listUserRoles(userId);
await ctx.auth.assignRoles(userId, ['role_id'], { reason: 'discord guild role match' });
await ctx.auth.removeRoles(userId, ['role_id'], { reason: 'discord guild role removed' });
```

This is the only supported way for a plugin to change roles. `user.write`
cannot.

## 5. Show link state on the profile

Mount a card on the `profile-connections` slot so a signed-in user can link
and unlink. See [Frontend](/api/plugins/frontend/). discord-oauth is the
reference implementation.

## Store the link

Keep the external account id in a `dedicated` collection, not in a user
column. You cannot add columns. discord-oauth and oidc-sso both set
`"storageEngine": "dedicated"` and key documents by the panel user id plus
the provider subject.

## Related

- [Plugin Backend](/api/plugins/backend/) — routes, auth modes, and the grant model
- [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) — declaring `authProviders` and permissions
- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the REST endpoints session and API-key auth apply to

# Plugin Licensing

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/plugins/licensing/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

A plugin can declare that it uses **vendor-owned licensing**: you issue and
validate license keys on your own license server, and you can ship the
plugin's valuable code encrypted so it only runs after activation. This page
is the contract for doing that — the manifest block, the activation wire
protocol, and the crypto, specified exactly so you can reimplement the server
side in any language.

## What Catalyst does and does not do

Catalyst is deliberately **not** a licensing authority. It never issues keys,
never validates them, and never sees one. Its jobs are exactly three:

1. Declare the phone-home in `plugin.json` so admins see it before enabling.
2. Hand the plugin a stable `ctx.installId`.
3. Refuse to install a package marked `licensing.encrypted` that ships no
   `backend/*.enc` payload.

| Catalyst does | Catalyst does not |
| --- | --- |
| Disclose the declared license server and contact hosts before enable | Issue, validate, or see license keys |
| Provide a stable per-panel `ctx.installId` for seat binding | Decrypt payloads or hold any vendor key |
| Enforce `licensing.encrypted` at install time | Guarantee the encrypted code never leaks (see [Threat model](/api/plugins/licensing/#threat-model)) |

Everything else — key issuance, seat accounting, revocation, payment — is
your code on your server.

## Manifest block

The block lives in `plugin.json` and is validated by the `PluginLicensingSchema`
in `catalyst-backend/src/plugins/validator.ts`. It is optional. **Presence of
the block is the flag** that the plugin contacts an external license server
and may ship an encrypted payload.

```json
"licensing": {
  "licenseServer": "https://licenses.vendor.example/v1/activate",
  "buyUrl": "https://vendor.example/buy",
  "contact": ["licenses.vendor.example"],
  "encrypted": true,
  "failMode": "closed",
  "cacheTtlHours": 168
}
```

| Field | Required | Default | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `licenseServer` | yes, when `licensing` is present | — | Must be `https`. Exception: `http` is accepted only for `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, and `::1` (any port) — local development only. Max 500 chars. |
| `buyUrl` | no | — | Same URL rule as `licenseServer`. Shown to admins when activation fails. |
| `contact` | no | the `licenseServer` hostname | Array of bare hostnames matching `^[a-z0-9.-]{1,253}$i`, max 8. This is what the consent dialog discloses. |
| `encrypted` | no | `false` | When `true`, the package MUST ship at least one `backend/*.enc` file or install fails with `PAYLOAD_MISSING`. |
| `failMode` | no | `closed` | One of `closed`, `open`. **Only meaningful when `encrypted` is false** — an encrypted plugin structurally cannot fall open (there is no key). `closed` throws on activation failure (the plugin stays disabled); `open` resolves `{ enabled: false }` so the plugin can degrade. |
| `cacheTtlHours` | no | `168` (7 days) | Integer 1–8760. |

## Consent disclosure

The panel's safety-consent dialog (shown before first enable) renders a
**Network & licensing** section whenever `licensing` is present. It shows:

- "Contacts `licenses.vendor.example` to validate a license" — the `contact`
  hosts.
- "Ships an encrypted payload. Its code is readable only after activation." —
  when `encrypted` is set.
- "Activation endpoint: `https://…`" — the `licenseServer`.
- A "Get a license" button — when `buyUrl` is set.

This rides the existing consent machinery (`permissionDescriptions` and the
`SAFETY_CONSENT_REQUIRED` response of `POST /api/plugins/:name/enable`).
Nothing about consent semantics changed.

## `ctx.installId`

The plugin backend context carries `installId`: a stable, opaque identity for
the panel install.

- Format: `inst_` plus 24 hex characters (12 random bytes), for example
  `inst_4f8a1c2e9b03d6a75c1e8f20`.
- Generated once, persisted in the `PanelIdentity` table, never rotates.
  It survives restarts and plugin reinstalls.
- It is an **identifier, not a secret**. Vendors bind seats to it. Do not
  derive anything sensitive from it, and do not treat it as one.

If a database is copied between panels, the id travels with it. License
caches keyed on an install id are rejected when the id no longer matches, so a
copied install re-activates instead of silently reusing someone else's cache.

## Wire protocol

Your license server implements `POST` at `licensing.licenseServer` with
`Content-Type: application/json`. The plugin sends:

```json
{
  "licenseKey": "VND1-K4M2Q-8XR7P-3TN9W-B5HD2",
  "installId": "inst_4f8a1c2e9b03d6a75c1e8f20",
  "pluginName": "licensed-example",
  "pluginVersion": "1.0.0"
}
```

`200 OK`:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "wrappedDek": "<base64url of nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag(16)>",
  "expiresAt": "2026-09-29T12:00:00.000Z",
  "entitlements": ["bzip2", "multi-node"],
  "seats": { "used": 1, "max": 1 }
}
```

Errors are all `{"ok":false,"code":"…"}`:

| Status | Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | `INVALID_KEY` | Key unknown or hash mismatch |
| 403 | `REVOKED` | Key explicitly revoked |
| 409 | `SEAT_EXHAUSTED` | Install not bound and no free seat |
| 409 | `VERSION_MISMATCH` | Key not entitled for this `pluginVersion` |
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | Missing or invalid fields |
| 413 | `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | Request body over 16 KB |
| 503 | `UNAVAILABLE` | Transient failure |
| 500 | `INTERNAL` | Unexpected error — never a stack trace |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Unknown route |

Other endpoints your server should implement:

| Endpoint | Body | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/deactivate` | `{licenseKey, installId}` | Frees a seat |
| `POST /v1/revoke` | `{licenseKey, reason}` | Revokes a key |
| `POST /v1/issue` | `{customerEmail, seats, entitlements, versions}` | Issues a key; the response contains the key **once** and it is never retrievable again |
| `GET /healthz` | — | Liveness probe |

## Crypto contract

This is exact. Reimplement it in any language from this section alone.

```text
KEK = HKDF-SHA256(
        ikm  = UTF-8(licenseKey),
        salt = UTF-8(installId),
        info = UTF-8("catalyst-catpkg-dek-wrap-v1"),
        len  = 32)

wrap = AES-256-GCM(KEK, DEK)
       AAD = UTF-8(pluginName + "\u0000" + pluginVersion)
       output = nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag(16), base64url-encoded
```

- The DEK is 32 random bytes, **one per plugin version**, rotated each
  release. It encrypts the payload at build time.
- The DEK travels to the plugin **wrapped**, never in the clear. A log leak or
  a MITM on the activation call cannot recover it.
- AES-GCM's auth tag is the integrity check: a forged `wrappedDek` fails to
  unwrap. No response signing is needed for the key path.
- A MITM on activation can only deny service, never forge an entitlement.

## Payload format

`backend/payload.enc` is one AES-256-GCM envelope. Key = the DEK.

| Offset | Length | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 12 | GCM nonce, random per build |
| 12 | n | ciphertext |
| end−16 | 16 | GCM auth tag |

- AAD = `UTF-8(pluginName ‖ "\0" ‖ pluginVersion)` — the same AAD as the wrap,
  so a payload cannot be transplanted across versions.
- The plaintext is **one bundled ESM module** with no bare imports (the same
  constraint as `frontend.mjs`, for the same reason: it is loaded from a
  `data:` URL).
- Export shape: `default` is the normal plugin object with `onLoad`,
  `onEnable`, `onDisable`, and `onUnload`.
- It is loaded via `import('data:text/javascript;base64,…')` so **plaintext
  never lands on disk** — the panel's hot-reload staging directory
  `…/.cache/backend/…` never sees the decrypted module.
- `plugin.json` is **always** plaintext. The panel must validate the manifest
  before anything runs.

## SDK

`@catalyst/plugin-sdk/licensing` is backend-only (it uses `node:crypto`).
**Bundle it into your bootstrap at build time** — plugin backends are
self-contained bundles (the same contract as `frontend.mjs`), so the SDK is
not a runtime dependency of the panel.

| Export | Job |
| --- | --- |
| `defineLicensing(def)` | Build the manifest block |
| `deriveKek(licenseKey, installId)` | 32-byte KEK |
| `licensingAad(pluginName, pluginVersion)` | AAD bytes |
| `wrapDek(kek, dek, aad)` / `unwrapDek(kek, wrappedDek, aad)` | Vendor side / plugin side |
| `decryptPayload(dek, payloadBytes, aad)` | Decrypt `backend/*.enc` to an ESM source string |
| `importPayload(code)` | Dynamic-import the module from a `data:` URL |
| `activateLicense(ctx, opts)` | The whole flow: read `config.licenseKey`, use the cached activation if fresh, else POST to `licenseServer`, unwrap, cache. Returns `{ enabled, dek, entitlements, expiresAt, cached, error? }` |
| `loadLicensedModule(ctx, { payload, … })` | One call: activate, decrypt, import, return the plugin object |

Types: `PluginLicensing`, `PluginRuntimeContext`, `ActivateOptions`,
`Activation`. `@catalyst/plugin-sdk/testing` also exports
`createMockLicense(opts)` for plugin tests.

A minimal bootstrap looks like this:

```javascript
// backend/index.js (built bootstrap)
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { loadLicensedModule } from '@catalyst/plugin-sdk/licensing';

let real;
async function boot(ctx) {
  if (!real) {
    real = await loadLicensedModule(ctx, {
      payload: new Uint8Array(readFileSync(new URL('./payload.enc', import.meta.url))),
    });
  }
  return real;
}
export default {
  async onLoad(ctx) { (await boot(ctx))?.onLoad?.(ctx); },
  // …onEnable / onDisable / onUnload
};
```

`activateLicense` reads the license key from `config.licenseKey` by default
(override with the `keyField` option), so declare a config field of type
`password` with that key and document it for the operator.

## Caching & outages

The activation is cached in the plugin's own storage at key
`licensing.activation` as
`{ installId, wrappedDek, expiresAt, entitlements, activatedAt }`.

- A cache record is **rejected when `installId` differs** from `ctx.installId`.
- It is **rejected when `expiresAt` is past** — then `activateLicense`
  reactivates against `licenseServer`.
- The plaintext DEK is **never** persisted. Only the wrapped key is stored.

Because the wrapped key is cached, a vendor outage does not become a panel
incident: the plugin keeps working until the cached activation expires
(`cacheTtlHours`, default 168). When activation does fail and there is no
fresh cache:

- `closed` (the default, and the only mode for an encrypted plugin) throws on
  activation failure — the plugin stays disabled.
- `open` (non-encrypted plugins only) resolves `{ enabled: false }` so the
  plugin can degrade gracefully.

## Threat model

**This is a deterrent, not DRM.** It deters package copying between panels,
key sharing across installs, casual patching, and unlicensed redistribution.

One sentence of rationale, because it shapes the whole design: plugins
already have unrestricted outbound network access (discord-oauth calls
Discord, ai-assistant calls OpenAI/Anthropic), so "let the plugin phone home"
required no new capability. What was missing is that it happened *silently*.
This feature makes it declared and disclosable.

**Caution**
**What this does NOT defend against:** an admin with database access, or a
determined cracker who dumps the decrypted module from the process. Plaintext
exists in memory and in the module cache. Importing via a `data:` URL avoids
*disk* exposure, which raises the bar from "read the staging directory" to
"attach a debugger" — that is the ceiling, and it is the right trade-off for
the goal.

**Frontend cannot be meaningfully encrypted.** `frontend.mjs` is served to the
browser; any key handed to the browser is the attacker's. Encrypt the
*backend* (the valuable logic) and ship a thin frontend shell that calls
backend routes. Do not spend effort encrypting the frontend.

## Reference implementations

Both live in the
[catalyst-plugins](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins) repository
and are meant to be copied:

- [tools/license-server](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/tools/license-server)
  — zero-dependency `node:http` reference vendor license server: issue,
  activate, deactivate, revoke, and healthz, with keys stored SHA-256-hashed,
  seat binding, and version matching.
- [licensed-example](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/tree/main/licensed-example)
  — the working client plugin: a plaintext `backend/index.js` bootstrap, an
  encrypted `backend/payload.enc`, and a `/premium-report` route that only
  exists after activation.

## Related

- [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) — the `licensing` block's validation
- [Packaging & marketplace](/api/plugins/packaging/) — shipping the encrypted payload
- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the panel REST API the plugin calls beside

---

# Packaging & Marketplace

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/plugins/packaging/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

Panels install plugins from a marketplace index. The official index is
[catalyst-plugins](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins) and is
browsed by default. You can run your own index without being listed there.

## Prerequisites

- A plugin directory with a valid `plugin.json` — see
  [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/).
- A Catalyst checkout to build the SDK CLI from; the CLI is not published to
  npm. See [Create a plugin](/api/plugins/creating/).
- HTTPS hosting for the package. Panels refuse plaintext `http` downloads from
  any host that is not a configured index host.

## Package layout

A `.catpkg.zip` is a zip whose entries sit at the archive root (one wrapper
folder is flattened). The installer allows only:

| Entry | Required |
| --- | --- |
| `plugin.json` | yes |
| `backend/` | no |
| `frontend/` | no |
| `assets/` | no |
| `README.md` | no |
| `LICENSE` | no |

Anything else is rejected, including `package.json`, `node_modules`, `src/`,
and dotfiles. `../`, absolute paths, and links that escape the plugin
directory are rejected before anything is written.

Limits: 256 MB compressed, 512 MB extracted, 20,000 entries.

A packaged `backend.entry` has to live under `backend/`, because that is the
only allowed top-level place for backend files — the installer drops the rest.
`dist/` is not an allowed top-level entry, so a scaffold's `dist/...` entry
cannot ship in a package. Official plugins author `backend/index.js` directly
and set `entry` to that path. If you did compile TypeScript, copy the output to
`backend/index.js` and point the manifest there before packing. (The loader
itself only requires `backend.entry` to resolve inside the plugin directory;
the top-level allowlist is what constrains the package.)

## Encrypted payloads

A package whose `plugin.json` sets `licensing.encrypted: true` must ship at
least one `backend/*.enc` payload. The installer refuses the package with
`PAYLOAD_MISSING` otherwise, so a mispackaged plugin fails at install time
instead of in front of an admin at enable time. `plugin.json` itself stays
plaintext — the panel validates it before anything runs. See
[Plugin licensing](/api/plugins/licensing/).

## Build the archive

The CLI ships in the Catalyst repository, not on npm, and nothing links its
binary, so invoke it by path. Build it once, then `pack` from the plugin
directory — see [Create a plugin](/api/plugins/creating/#1-scaffold) for why
there is no `catalyst-plugin` command on `PATH`:

```bash
# once, from the Catalyst checkout root
pnpm --filter @catalyst/plugin-sdk run build
pnpm --dir packages/plugin-sdk/cli run build

# from the plugin directory ($CATALYST_REPO is your checkout)
node "$CATALYST_REPO/packages/plugin-sdk/cli/dist/index.js" pack
node "$CATALYST_REPO/packages/plugin-sdk/cli/dist/index.js" pack --out dist
```

`pack` needs `archiver` resolvable — a devDependency of `packages/plugin-sdk`
that `pnpm install` hoists to the workspace root; without an install it prints
`archiver is unavailable`.

`pack` writes `<name>-<version>.catpkg.zip` and `<name>-<version>.catpkg.zip.sha256`.
It includes `plugin.json`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, and the `backend/`,
`frontend/`, and `assets/` directories when they exist. It does not compile
TypeScript and it does not build `frontend.mjs`. Do both before packing. A
package with neither `backend/` nor `frontend/` installs and does nothing.

The official repository does the same thing with `zip` and then rewrites
`index.json`:

```bash
# from a plugin directory — matches scripts/build-packages.sh
zip -qr ../my-plugin-1.0.0.catpkg.zip plugin.json backend frontend README.md \
  -x '*/node_modules/*' -x '*/.*' -x 'frontend/dist/*'
sha256sum ../my-plugin-1.0.0.catpkg.zip
```

## Index document

Serve JSON over HTTPS. The panel accepts either a bare array or:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "my-plugin",
      "displayName": "My Plugin",
      "description": "What an admin reads in the marketplace list.",
      "author": "Your Name",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "downloadUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/my-plugin-1.0.0.catpkg.zip",
      "sha256": "hex digest of the zip",
      "homepage": "https://github.com/you/my-plugin",
      "tags": ["notifications"]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | yes | Must equal the packaged plugin's `plugin.json` name. |
| `downloadUrl` | yes | Absolute URL of the `.catpkg.zip`. |
| `sha256` | yes in practice | Lowercase hex digest of the zip. The panel lists an entry without it but refuses to install it (`CHECKSUM_REQUIRED`). |
| `version` | no | Shown in the version column; drives the update badge. |
| `displayName`, `description`, `author`, `homepage` | no | Display only. |
| `tags` | no | Filter chips in the marketplace; the first 12 strings are kept. |
| `licensing` | no | `{ licenseServer, buyUrl, encrypted }` for the browse badge. The installed `plugin.json` is authoritative. |

`sha256` is a hard requirement for installation: the panel verifies the
downloaded bytes against it before extracting anything, and a missing or
mismatched digest aborts the install.

`downloadUrl` must be `https`. Two exceptions are treated as trusted: a host
that is also one of your configured index hosts, and any host when the panel
sets `PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_ALLOW_LOCAL=true`. Hosts that resolve to loopback,
link-local, or private addresses are refused in the same cases.

Redirects are followed up to 5 hops, and the protocol and private-address
checks are re-applied to every hop, so a public URL cannot redirect the
download at an internal address. Index URLs themselves are fetched as-is,
including LAN hosts, because an admin configured them.

The panel caches each index for 5 minutes; browsing with a forced refresh
sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`. One failing source does not hide the others.

## Point a panel at your index

An admin adds the URL in the **Marketplaces** rail of
**Admin → Extensions → Marketplace**, or sets environment variables on the
backend:

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_URLS` | Comma-separated extra index URLs, browsed together with the official index. |
| `PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL` | `true` skips the official index. Use on air-gapped installs. |
| `PLUGIN_MARKETPLACE_ALLOW_LOCAL` | `true` permits plaintext `http` downloads and loopback/private hosts other than your configured index hosts. Leave unset on a public panel. |

When two sources list the same `name`, the newest `version` wins.

## Install, update, uninstall

All three are clicks in **Admin → Extensions** — the operator steps live in
[Plugins](/admin/plugins/#update-reload-disable-uninstall). What matters when
you publish:

- The panel downloads the zip, verifies `sha256`, extracts, and validates
  `plugin.json`. The code lands on disk **not running**.
- An admin then enables it and accepts the safety disclaimer.
- A higher `version` in the index offers **Update**, which replaces the
directory. A version or permission change forces the disclaimer again and
  leaves the plugin disabled until it is accepted.

`POST /api/plugins/install` with `{ "url", "sha256" }` is the same flow;
`sha256` is a required 64-hex digest. `POST /api/plugins/:name/reload`
re-reads the directory without a panel restart.

## Get listed officially

Third-party indexes do not need anyone's approval. To land in the official
index, open a pull request on
[catalystctl/catalyst-plugins](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins)
that adds one directory:

- Directory name equals `plugin.json` `name`.
- `backend.entry` and `frontend.entry` point at files that exist.
- An `index.json` entry with the same `name` and `version`. CI rejects a
  mismatch either way.
- UI plugins include a `vite.config.mts` that emits `frontend/frontend.mjs`.
  CI runs `scripts/build-bundles.mjs` before packing.

CI packs every directory that contains `plugin.json`, writes the sha256 back
into `index.json`, and publishes the zips on the `dist` branch. Download URLs
look like:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/catalystctl/catalyst-plugins/dist/plugins/<name>-<version>.catpkg.zip
```

## Verify

After enable:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $CATALYST_API_KEY" \
  https://panel.example.com/api/plugins/my-plugin
```

The response includes the manifest, whether consent is current, and the
granted permissions. Then call one of your own routes and confirm a disabled
plugin returns `503` rather than running the handler.

## Related

- [Plugin Manifest](/api/plugins/manifest/) — the fields the installer validates
- [Create a plugin](/api/plugins/creating/) — scaffold and build the plugin first
- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the panel REST API the marketplace endpoints sit beside

# API Reference

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/api/reference/
Audience: developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

This reference is **generated** from the backend's route definitions
(`catalyst-backend/scripts/export-openapi.ts` → `api/openapi.json`), so it
tracks the code instead of drifting from it. Every operation also carries an
`x-catalyst` block with the `source` file and line, the `permissionGuards` it
enforces, and the `errorCodes` it can return.

**Note**
The contract also lists the long-lived SSE endpoints (console, server events,
metrics, admin events, node agent logs) with their status codes. The event names
and payloads they push are in [Realtime events](/api/websockets/).

**Note**
The viewer loads from a CDN with JavaScript enabled. Offline or script-blocked
readers can use the raw [openapi.json](/openapi.json) with any OpenAPI tool.

# Overview

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/overview/
Audience: user, admin
Last verified: 2026-10-20

When something breaks, start with the layer that owns the symptom:

| Symptom | Go to |
| --- | --- |
| One game server crashes, will not start, or misbehaves | [Server issues](/troubleshooting/server/) |
| A whole node is unreachable or all its servers suffer | [Node issues](/troubleshooting/node/) |
| The panel itself errors, logins fail, pages break | [Panel issues](/troubleshooting/panel/) |
| Players cannot connect but everything looks green | [Networking issues](/troubleshooting/networking/) |
| A specific error message | [Common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) |

Administrators can also capture a redacted bundle of panel, node, and server
logs in one step — see [diagnostics bundle](/troubleshooting/diagnostics-bundle/).

## How to report a problem well

Whether you ask your administrator, your host, or the community, include:

1. **What you expected** vs. **what happened** (one sentence each).
2. **The exact error text** — copy, do not paraphrase. Codes from
   [common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) speed everything up.
3. **When** it started and **what changed** just before (updates, new mods,
   config edits, new server).
4. **Scope**: one server, all servers on a node, or the whole panel.

"The server is broken" takes five follow-up questions. The four facts above
usually get an answer in one round.

---

# Server Issues

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/server/
Audience: user, admin
Last verified: 2026-10-16

## Prerequisites

- Access to the game server as its owner or as a subuser with the permissions
  the fix needs (console, power, files, startup).
- For node-level causes (full disk, OOM killer), an administrator for the node
  that hosts the server.

## Crash loop (starts, then stops)

1. Open the server's **Console** tab and press **Start** — the first error after
   start is the cause; everything after is fallout.
2. Usual suspects in order:
   - A config or startup variable you just changed → revert it ([startup](/users/startup/)).
   - A new/updated mod or plugin → remove it and restart ([mods](/users/mods-plugins/)).
   - Minecraft shows a **Minecraft EULA** prompt → select **I Agree**, then
     start again.
   - Out of memory → the game asked for more than the server owns; lower the
     game's memory setting or raise the server limit.
3. If nothing changed and it suddenly loops, check whether the **node** is
   unhealthy ([node issues](/troubleshooting/node/)) — full disks and OOM
   killers look like game crashes.

## Stuck "starting" or "stopping"

1. Wait 60–90 seconds; large worlds save slowly.
2. Use **Kill** if **Stop** hangs, then **Start** again
   ([power controls](/users/power/)).
3. Repeated hangs on stop point at a mod blocking shutdown — remove suspects
   one by one.

## Port already in use

Two servers claim the same allocation, or a killed server did not release its
port. The panel rejects the change with `PORT_ALREADY_IN_USE` ("Port N is
already in use on this node"). Confirm no other server uses that IP + port
([networking](/users/networking/)), kill any ghost process via the node, and
restart. If it persists, the administrator must free the allocation.

## Files tab hangs, times out, or returns empty files

Every listing, download and upload in the **Files** tab is relayed by the panel
to the node agent, so the failure is usually the node rather than the file:

- "The node is offline and cannot accept this action." (`NODE_OFFLINE`) — see
  [node issues](/troubleshooting/node/).
- "The agent did not respond in time." (`AGENT_TIMEOUT`) — retry once, then
  check the node's load and free disk.
- "The file tunnel is busy. Please try again later." (`FILE_TUNNEL_BUSY`) — too
  many file operations are queued for that node; wait for in-flight transfers
  to finish.

If the node is healthy, check the panel version: listings that timed out
without a node error were fixed in v1.79.4, and files that opened or downloaded
empty were fixed in v1.81.0. Update the panel
([updating Catalyst](/admin/updating/)).

## Lag with normal-looking settings

1. Check **Metrics**: memory pressure, CPU saturation, or disk latency.
2. Reduce view distance / loaded chunks / entity counts before buying bigger limits.
3. Rule out the network path ([networking issues](/troubleshooting/networking/)) —
   server TPS fine + players rubber-banding means transit, not the server.

## Nuclear option

When the install itself is damaged: [back up](/users/backups/), then
[reinstall](/users/reinstalling/). Faster than archaeology for mangled installs.

## Related

- [Common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) — look up a code or message.
- [Node issues](/troubleshooting/node/) — every server on the node is affected.
- [Networking issues](/troubleshooting/networking/) — players cannot reach the server.
- [Backups](/users/backups/) — back up before reinstalling or making risky changes.

---

# Networking Issues

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/networking/
Audience: user, admin
Last verified: 2026-10-20

## Prerequisites

- A running game server whose allocation you can read from the panel.
- For the node and TLS sections: shell access on the node, and access to the
  install directory to read the `.env` and view proxy logs.

## Players cannot reach a game server

1. Is the server **running**? A stopped server refuses everything.
2. Is the address right — IP **and** port? Retype it; do not trust memory. The
   **Address** column in **Servers** and the server's **Admin** tab show its
   allocations.
3. Is the port reachable from outside? Test from a different network (mobile data
   works). "Works on my LAN, not from outside" means NAT or firewall, not the game.
4. **UDP vs TCP**: many games need UDP. A TCP-only port check passing proves
   nothing for a UDP game.
5. Host firewall, cloud security group, and any NAT rule must all agree, and the
   allocation must be published on the node. The node agent creates the port
   mapping and firewall rule for each allocation; a rule that failed to apply
   looks exactly like a closed firewall.

## Game ports on firewalld hosts

On `firewalld` the agent adds the runtime rule first (reachable immediately) and
then the permanent rule (survives a reboot), without reloading the daemon. Two
failures remain:

```bash
sudo firewall-cmd --list-ports            # runtime rules
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --list-ports # rules kept across reboot
```

- The allocation is missing from both lists → the runtime add failed. The agent
  log has `firewalld runtime add failed for <port>/<proto>`; fix the `firewall-cmd`
  error it quotes (SELinux denial, read-only zone, missing capability).
- The port works until the node reboots → only the runtime half landed. The agent
  log warns `firewalld could not persist port <port>/<proto>`; re-add it with
  `sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=<port>/tcp` (and `/udp`) then
  `sudo firewall-cmd --reload`.

## Panel unreachable from another machine

The installer never changes the host firewall: it only reports whether the panel
port is allowed and prints the command. On `firewalld` hosts (Fedora Server,
RHEL, CentOS):

```bash
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8080/tcp && sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

On `ufw` hosts: `sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp`. Use your own `FRONTEND_PORT` if you
changed it ([installation](/admin/installation/)). If the panel works on the host
itself but not from another machine, this — or an upstream cloud security group —
is the cause.

## Node cannot reach the panel

Resolve the panel hostname from the node, then `curl` the panel URL: DNS first,
then TLS (cert valid for that name?), then HTTP. See
[node issues](/troubleshooting/node/).

## Panel loads but every API call returns 502

The page renders — static files come from the frontend container — but sign-in,
the server list, and realtime all fail, because the frontend's nginx cannot
resolve the backend. nginx names the failure in its own log:

```bash
docker compose logs frontend | grep -i 'backend could not be resolved'
```

- **Bundled stack** — nginx proxies to the fixed service name `backend`, which it
  resolves once at startup. A renamed or moved backend service stops the frontend
  from starting; restore the service name.
- **Frontend image run directly** (Podman, Kubernetes, host networking) — the
  resolver comes from the frontend container's own `/etc/resolv.conf`, so a
  backend name that only resolves through a search domain fails. Set
  `BACKEND_HOST` to the fully qualified name, and `NGINX_LOCAL_RESOLVERS` when its
  nameservers are wrong.

A `wget http://backend:3000/health` that succeeds inside the frontend container
while nginx logs a resolve failure is the signature of a resolver mismatch.

## TLS warnings in browsers

- Name mismatch: the certificate must cover exactly the host users type — set
  `PUBLIC_URL` in the install `.env` to that `https://` URL.
- Expired: renewal failed — is port 80 reachable, did DNS change? Check the TLS
  overlay's logs (`docker compose logs caddy` or `traefik`), not the backend.

## SFTP times out

SFTP runs on the **node agent** (default port **2022**), not on the panel, and is
separate from game ports. Confirm the port is written into the agent config on the
node, reachable through every firewall layer (the agent opens it on the node's
firewall when it starts), and that the client uses SFTP (SSH transport), not FTP.
Details: [SFTP](/users/sftp/).

## Related

- [Common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) — look up a code or message.
- [Node issues](/troubleshooting/node/) — the node cannot reach the panel or its agent is down.
- [Panel issues](/troubleshooting/panel/) — rule out the panel before chasing the network.
- [Server networking](/users/networking/) — allocate and edit server ports.
