# Common Errors

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/common-errors/
Audience: user, admin, developer
Last verified: 2026-10-20

This page maps what you **see** to what to do. The panel and API attach a stable
`code` to most errors — look yours up in [API errors](/api/errors/) for the HTTP
status and whether it is safe to retry. Branch on the `code`, never on the
message: messages are localized and may change.

## Symptom guide

| What you see | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "You do not have permission to perform this action." (`PERMISSION_DENIED`) | Signed in, but not allowed. | Check your role or subuser grants ([authorization](/api/authorization/), [subusers](/users/subusers/)). |
| "Some of the provided values are invalid." (`VALIDATION_ERROR`) | A field was rejected. | Fix the highlighted field; for API calls read `details` for the offending fields. |
| "That value is already taken." (`CONFLICT`) | A unique value (usually the name) exists. | Rename, or delete the conflicting resource first. |
| "The requested resource could not be found." (`NOT_FOUND`) | It was deleted, or it is hidden from your account. | Check the ID and confirm it still exists. |
| "Too many requests. Please wait a moment and try again." (`RATE_LIMITED`) | You are over a rate limit. | Back off, stop polling ([rate limits](/api/rate-limits/)). |
| "The node does not have enough resources for this action." (`INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`) | The node lacks memory, CPU, disk, or free allocations. | Free capacity or ask the administrator for a bigger node. |
| `Port {{port}} is already in use on this node.` (`PORT_ALREADY_IN_USE`) | Two servers claim the same allocation. | [Server issues](/troubleshooting/server/) — free or reassign the port. |
| "The server must be stopped for this action (current state: …)." (`SERVER_NOT_STOPPED`) | The action needs the server off. | **Stop** the server, then retry. |
| "The node is offline and cannot accept this action." (`NODE_OFFLINE`) | The node's agent is not reachable. | [Node issues](/troubleshooting/node/). |
| "The agent did not respond in time." (`AGENT_TIMEOUT`) | The agent did not answer within the request timeout. | Retry once, then check node load and free disk. |
| "This server is suspended." (`SERVER_SUSPENDED`) | Suspension is enforced on the panel. | Ask the administrator to unsuspend it. |
| "This account is temporarily locked after too many failed sign-in attempts." (`ACCOUNT_LOCKED`) | Sign-in lockout. | Wait for the lockout to expire, or ask an administrator. |
| "This account has been suspended." (`ACCOUNT_BANNED`) | The account is banned. | Ask an administrator. |
| Minecraft **Minecraft EULA** dialog | The EULA is not accepted yet. | Select **I Agree**, then start the server ([first server](/getting-started/first-server/)). |
| SFTP client reports "authentication failed" | Stale or mistyped credentials. | Copy fresh credentials from the **SFTP** tab ([SFTP](/users/sftp/)). |

If your message is not here, open **Admin → System Errors** to see the persisted
exception, or capture a [diagnostics bundle](/troubleshooting/diagnostics-bundle/).

## Related

- [API errors](/api/errors/) — the full stable-code table: statuses, meanings, retry guidance.
- [Troubleshooting overview](/troubleshooting/overview/) — start from the layer that owns the symptom.

---

# Node Issues

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/node/
Audience: admin
Last verified: 2026-10-20

## Prerequisites

- Admin access to the panel, so you can read node status, metrics, and logs.
- Shell access on the node (root or a sudo-capable account) to inspect and
  restart `catalyst-agent`.

## Node shows unreachable

Running servers keep running — only management is down. Check in order:

1. **Agent process** on the node: `systemctl status catalyst-agent` (or the
   OpenRC equivalent). Restart it and watch its logs:
   `journalctl -u catalyst-agent -n 100 --no-pager`.
2. **Node → panel path**: DNS resolves the panel URL from the node? Outbound
   HTTPS reaches it? A proxy or firewall change breaks this silently.
3. **Panel side**: is the panel itself healthy ([panel issues](/troubleshooting/panel/))?
   An unreachable panel makes every node look dead.
4. **Credentials**: rotated or revoked node API keys break check-in — re-register
   the key ([registering](/admin/nodes/registering/)).

## Agent installed but never checks in

- Wrong panel URL (scheme/host/port) in the agent config — the most common cause.
- Clock skew: large time differences break TLS and token validation; sync with NTP.
- Version mismatch: an agent far newer/older than the panel may be rejected —
  keep them in step ([updating a node](/admin/nodes/updating/)).

## Agent unit will not start (SELinux label, start limit)

If `systemctl status catalyst-agent` shows the unit failing within a second or
restarting forever, check the exact exit reason in
`journalctl -u catalyst-agent -n 50 --no-pager`:

- **`status=203/EXEC` with `Permission denied`** — the binary carries the wrong
  SELinux label. Agents installed before v1.85.0 were moved into place from
  `/tmp`, which keeps the source label (`user_tmp_t`), and systemd may not execute
  that. Re-run the node install command from the panel — it runs
  `deploy-agent.sh`, which now installs with `install(1)` and calls `restorecon`
  ([installing a node](/admin/nodes/installing/)) — or fix it in place:
  `sudo restorecon -F /opt/catalyst-agent/catalyst-agent && sudo systemctl restart catalyst-agent`.
- **`start request repeated too quickly`** — the unit hit its crash-loop bound
  (10 starts per 60 s) instead of restarting silently forever. Fix the underlying
  start failure above, then clear the counter with
  `sudo systemctl reset-failed catalyst-agent && sudo systemctl start catalyst-agent`.

A node running agent v1.85.0 or later bounds the loop this way; an older unit
keeps retrying forever and buries the real error in the journal.

## All servers on one node suffer

That is a node problem, not N server problems. Check node metrics first (disk
full, memory exhausted), consider rolling back a recent OS/runtime/agent update
([updating a node](/admin/nodes/updating/)), and migrate critical servers to a
healthy node while you investigate.

## Servers fail to start on one node

Creating and installing work, but every start fails on the same node. Check the
agent log on the node for one of these:

1. **`Cannot mount disk image for <server-uuid> ... Using the plain data
   directory; disk quota will not be enforced.`** — the node cannot create loop
   mounts (the underlying error contains `not permitted`, `Permission denied`,
   or `EPERM`). The agent deliberately continues with a plain data directory
   instead of refusing to start, so servers still run — but disk quota is
   **not enforced** on this node. If a later start also logs
   `Migration directory already exists: <path>`, remove the stale
   `<data-dir>/migrate/<server-uuid>` directory (default data dir
   `/var/lib/catalyst`) and start the server again.
2. **`io.weight` / cgroup IO error from `runc`** — the `io` cgroup v2
   controller is not delegated to the agent, so the runtime cannot apply the
   server's IO weight. This is common inside an unprivileged container. Run the
   node on a host (or a privileged container) whose cgroup v2 lists `io` in
   `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers`. The agent omits the IO weight
   automatically when the controller is absent, so keep the agent up to date.
3. A `SERVER_NOT_STOPPED` / "Server must be stopped" message is **not** a node
   fault — that check runs in the panel.

An unprivileged LXC container is the usual cause of 1 and 2. It can host a node,
but expect no disk quota and verify the `io` controller is available before
offering the node to users.

## Backup restores fail with "Function not implemented"

On Fedora 44 every archive restore aborts with `Function not implemented`
(`ENOSYS`) and the server returns to **Stopped** with that error. Fedora's GNU
tar issues `openat2(2)` when extracting, and systemd's `RestrictSUIDSGID=yes`
denies that syscall outright: classic seccomp cannot inspect the mode field
inside `struct open_how`, so systemd blocks the whole call
([systemd#43314](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/43314), closed
upstream as "fix in GNU tar").

The agent unit therefore ships `RestrictSUIDSGID=no`. Every other sandbox
directive stays on (`SystemCallFilter=@system-service @mount`,
`NoNewPrivileges=true`, `ProtectSystem=full`, `ProtectHome=true`,
`RestrictNamespaces=mnt net uts ipc`, the capability bounding set), and the
archive path keeps its own protections: restores refuse archive-supplied
ownership and permissions, refuse device entries and any member or link that
would escape the server directory before extraction, and game servers run as
unprivileged container users. Symbolic and hard links inside the server
directory restore normally — see [backups](/users/backups/).

1. **Confirm the cause** — on the node run
   `systemd-run -p RestrictSUIDSGID=yes --wait --pipe tar -cf /dev/null -C /tmp .`.
   On Fedora 44 it fails; the agent log shows the same error for the restore.
2. **Check the effective unit** — `systemctl show catalyst-agent -p RestrictSUIDSGID`
   must print `RestrictSUIDSGID=no`. Drop-ins override the main unit, so also run
   `grep -r RestrictSUIDSGID /etc/systemd/system/catalyst-agent.service.d/`.
3. **Apply the fix** — the agent repairs an upgraded-in-place node on its next
   start: it writes
   `/etc/systemd/system/catalyst-agent.service.d/zz-catalyst-openat2-compat.conf`
   and restarts once. To do it immediately, re-run the deploy script for the
   node, or set `RestrictSUIDSGID=no` in the unit and any drop-in, then
   `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart catalyst-agent`.

## Data to collect before asking for help

Agent version (`catalyst-agent --version`), the agent log tail
(`journalctl -u catalyst-agent -n 100 --no-pager`), node OS and free resources
(`df -h`, `free -m`), and whether the panel URL is reachable from the node with
`curl`. The [diagnostics bundle](/troubleshooting/diagnostics-bundle/) collects
all of this in one redacted file.

## Related

- [Common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) — look up a code or message.
- [Panel issues](/troubleshooting/panel/) — rule out the panel before blaming the node.
- [Networking issues](/troubleshooting/networking/) — the node cannot reach the panel.
- [Diagnostics bundle](/troubleshooting/diagnostics-bundle/) — collect node and panel logs together.

# Panel Issues

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/panel/
Audience: admin
Last verified: 2026-10-20

## Prerequisites

- Admin access to the panel, so you can open **Admin → System Errors** and
  **Admin → Audit Logs**.
- Shell access on the host running the stack, to read container logs and run
  `docker compose`.

## Install stopped on Fedora or RHEL (dnf5)

Fedora 41+ and RHEL/CentOS Stream 10 ship dnf5, which dropped the dnf4
`config-manager --add-repo` command the installer used to add Docker's
repository. An `install.sh` older than v1.85.0 aborts at that step, so Docker is
never installed and the stack is never created.

1. Re-download the current installer (v1.85.0 or later) and run it again. It
   detects dnf5, installs `dnf5-plugins` and uses
   `dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=`; on dnf4 it keeps using
   `dnf-plugins-core` and `--add-repo`.
2. To repair an old script by hand:
   `sudo dnf install -y dnf5-plugins` and
   `sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://download.docker.com/linux/fedora/docker-ce.repo`
   (use the `centos` path on RHEL/CentOS), then re-run the installer.

## Panel will not start after an update

1. Read the backend container logs first (`docker compose logs backend` from the
   install directory). Most failures announce themselves: a migration waiting on
   a lock, a renamed environment variable (check the release notes), or an
   unreachable database.
2. Confirm the PostgreSQL and Redis containers are up (`docker compose ps`) before
   blaming the backend.
3. Roll back per [updating Catalyst](/admin/updating/) if the cause is not obvious
   within minutes — a down panel blocks all management.

## HTTP 500s in the UI

- One page broken, the rest fine: open **Admin → System Errors** and filter by
  **Component** to see the persisted exception, then check backend logs at that
  timestamp. A missing column after a partial migration looks exactly like this —
  never interrupt migrations.
- Everything broken: database or Redis connectivity. Verify credentials,
  connectivity, and free disk on the database host.

## Nobody can log in

1. Can you reach the panel URL at all? If not, this is
   [networking](/troubleshooting/networking/), not auth.
2. Wrong password for everyone including admins: check the backend logs for
   auth/database errors rather than resetting passwords blindly. Sign-in failures
   are recorded in **Admin → Audit Logs** as `login_failed`.
3. Invites or resets never arrive: mail configuration
   ([configuration](/admin/configuration/)), spam folders, then mail provider
   logs.

## Pages load but data is stale

The UI caches aggressively. Hard-refresh, then check whether realtime streams are
connecting ([realtime events](/api/websockets/)) — a broken event stream looks
like frozen data while REST keeps working.

## Collect for a bug report

Panel version, browser and version, exact steps, backend log lines for the
incident window, and whether the problem survives a private window (rules out
extensions and cookies). **Admin → System Errors → Download diagnostics** captures
panel, node, and server logs in one redacted ZIP — see
[diagnostics bundle](/troubleshooting/diagnostics-bundle/).

## Related

- [Common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) — look up a code or message.
- [Node issues](/troubleshooting/node/) — the panel is healthy but nodes are not.
- [Networking issues](/troubleshooting/networking/) — the panel URL is unreachable.

---

# Diagnostics Bundle

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/troubleshooting/diagnostics-bundle/
Audience: admin
Last verified: 2026-10-20

When a problem spans layers — a panel error, a node that keeps disconnecting, and
one misbehaving game server — collecting each log by hand is slow and easy to get
wrong. The diagnostics bundle gathers everything for a time window into a single
ZIP, with secret values redacted.

## What the bundle contains

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `panel/logs.txt` | Panel container output for the window |
| `panel/environment.txt` | Effective panel configuration, secrets redacted |
| `panel/system-errors.json` | Persisted system errors for the window |
| `nodes/<nodeId>.log` | Node agent logs for the window |
| `servers/<serverId>/console.log` | Server console output for the window |
| `servers/<serverId>/.env` | The server's `.env`, when present, secrets redacted |
| `manifest.json` | Machine-readable index, counts, and collection warnings |
| `README.txt` | Human-readable summary of the same |

Every section is best-effort. A node that is offline, an agent that times out, or
a panel deployed without a container runtime shows up as a warning in
`manifest.json` instead of failing the whole export — read the warnings before
concluding that an empty file means "nothing happened". Collection is capped:
5,000 lines per node log, 8 MB per node and per server log, 20,000 server log rows,
and 10,000 system errors (a cap adds a warning).

## Prerequisites

- `admin.read` on the panel (the bundle crosses tenant boundaries by design, so
  it is admin-only).
- For the script: `curl` and network access to the panel — or directly to the
  backend when the frontend is down.

## Export from the panel

1. Open **Admin → System Errors**.
2. Select **Download diagnostics** (not **Export**, which writes only the system
   errors as Markdown or JSON). The dialog is also titled **Download diagnostics**.
3. Pick a **Time range**: **Last 1 hour**, **Last 6 hours**, **Last 24 hours**
   (default), **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, or **Custom** (**From**/**To**
   fields appear).
4. Under **Nodes** and **Servers**, leave **Select all** ticked to include
   everything, or untick it to choose specific entities. The server list has a
   search box.
5. Under **Redaction**, choose **Standard — keep IPs and hostnames** (default) or
   **Strict — mask IPs and hostnames**. Under **Sections**, leave the defaults
   (**Panel logs**, **System errors**, **Node logs**, **Server logs**,
   **Config & .env**) or untick what you do not need.
6. Select **Download**. The browser saves
   `catalyst-diagnostics-<timestamp>.zip`.

## Export with the script

Use this when the panel UI is broken or you are working from a terminal. It calls
the API directly, so it does not need the frontend.

```bash
bash collect-diagnostics.sh \
  --url https://panel.example.com \
  --api-key catalyst_your_admin_key \
  --hours 24
```

Without a checkout:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/catalystctl/catalyst/main/scripts/collect-diagnostics.sh \
  | bash -s -- --url https://panel.example.com --api-key catalyst_your_admin_key
```

Flags:

- `--hours N` — window size, 1 to 720. Default `24`.
- `--servers a,b` / `--nodes a,b` — limit the export; pass `none` to omit.
- `--sections panel,errors,nodes,servers,env` — include only what you need.
- `--redaction strict` — also mask IPs and hostnames.
- `--out FILE` — output path.
- `--cookie VALUE` — raw `Cookie` header for a browser session, as an alternative
  to `--api-key`.
- `--timeout SECONDS` — request timeout. Default `900`.
- `-k` — skip TLS verification for a self-signed certificate.

If the frontend is down but the backend port is reachable on the host, target the
backend directly:

```bash
bash collect-diagnostics.sh --url http://localhost:3000 --api-key catalyst_your_admin_key
```

### Equivalent raw API call

```bash
curl -fL \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer catalyst_your_admin_key" \
  "https://panel.example.com/api/admin/diagnostics/export?hours=24&redaction=standard" \
  -o catalyst-diagnostics.zip
```

Accepted query parameters: `hours` (default `24`, clamped 1–720), `from` and `to`
(ISO 8601; `from` overrides `hours`), `nodes`, `servers` (comma-separated IDs, or
`all` / `none`), `redaction` (`standard` or `strict`), and `sections` (any of
`panel,errors,nodes,servers,env`).

## Host-level collection

The panel bundle cannot see the host filesystem: the install `.env`, Compose
status, install logs, and container runtime health all live on the host, outside
the backend container.

For that layer run the script that ships with the install directory, on the host.
`install.sh` writes the stack to `catalyst-docker/` in the directory you ran it
from (usually `~/catalyst-docker`):

```bash
cd ~/catalyst-docker
bash diagnose.sh --lines=500
```

Flags use `=`: `--lines=N` (default 500, `--full` raises it to 2000 and adds
container inspect output), `--out=DIR`, `--compose-dir=DIR`, `--mask-hosts` (also
mask IPs and domains), `--full`, and `--skip-agent`. It writes
`catalyst-diagnostics-<timestamp>/catalyst-diagnostics-<timestamp>.txt` plus a
matching `.tar.gz` — one redacted text bundle, not the ZIP the panel produces.

Attach both when the problem could be either the panel logic or the host
configuration.

## Redaction

- **standard** (default) — secrets are replaced with `[REDACTED]`: passwords,
  tokens, API keys, license keys, cookies, and credentials inside connection URLs.
  IPs and hostnames are **kept**, because routing, CORS, and agent connectivity
  problems are much harder to diagnose without them.
- **strict** — everything standard does, plus IPs become `[IP_REDACTED]` and
  hostnames `[HOST_REDACTED]`.

Host masking is pattern-based: IP literals and hostnames ending in a well-known
TLD (`.com`, `.net`, `.io`, `.local`, `.internal`, …). An unusual internal domain
can survive strict mode.

The host-level `diagnose.sh` strips secrets by default too; `--mask-hosts` is its
equivalent of strict mode.

**Caution**
Redaction covers known secret patterns, not customer data. Review `manifest.json`
and a few log lines before attaching the bundle to a public issue or ticket.

## Related

- [Common errors](/troubleshooting/common-errors/) — look up a code before exporting.
- [Panel issues](/troubleshooting/panel/) — the export entry point lives in **Admin → System Errors**.

# Docs Contributor Guide

URL: https://docs.catalystctl.com/contributing/docs/
Audience: developer, admin
Last verified: 2026-10-20

## Prerequisites

- A clone of the docs repository (this site's source).
- Node.js ≥ 20 and pnpm. The repository pins `pnpm@9.15.9` in `packageManager`.

## Edit

Docs are Markdown/MDX under `src/content/docs/`, organized by audience:
`getting-started/`, `users/`, `admin/`, `api/`, `troubleshooting/`,
`contributing/`. Every page except the splash `index.mdx` needs all six
frontmatter fields:

```yaml
---
title: Creating Backups
description: One line saying what the page teaches.
audience:              # user, admin, developer — first entry is the primary audience
  - user
features:              # one or more tags from the canonical vocabulary
  - backups
sources:               # repo paths whose changes should trigger review
  - catalyst-backend/src/routes/backups.ts
last_verified: YYYY-MM-DD   # bump only when you verify against source
---
```

Rules: task-oriented prose, one **primary** audience per page (the first
frontmatter entry — add more only when the task genuinely spans them), Catalyst
terminology (`panel`, `node`, `server`, `template`, `allocation`, `task` — never
reuse the Pterodactyl product name for a Catalyst server, and never call a server
*a container* or *an instance*; *container* only means the Docker/OCI runtime
object), and no invented flags, ports, or defaults.

[`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst-doc/blob/main/AGENTS.md) is
the authoritative contract — it holds the per-field requirements, the canonical
30-tag `features` vocabulary that `scripts/validate-docs.mjs` enforces, and the
aside syntax (`:::note[Title]`, no space after `:::`; kinds `note`, `tip`,
`caution`, `danger`). A new page also needs a sidebar entry in
`astro.config.mjs`; the sidebar is nested (Starlight `items:` groups) and nesting
does not change URLs.

## Validate

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # preview at http://localhost:4321
pnpm validate     # links, slugs, frontmatter, features, assets, OpenAPI, terminology
pnpm test         # docs-agent unit tests
pnpm run build    # the same command Cloudflare Pages runs
```

The checks are plain Node scripts, runnable without the pnpm aliases:

```bash
node scripts/validate-docs.mjs      # pnpm validate
node scripts/check-terminology.mjs  # pnpm check-terminology
node scripts/sync-openapi.mjs --check
```

Fix every failure — CI runs `pnpm validate --strict` on every pull request, which
also turns an orphan page (one no sidebar entry reaches) into a failure.

## API reference

Never hand-edit `api/openapi.json` or `public/openapi.json`. Regenerate from a
Catalyst checkout (`--from-checkout` runs that repo's `openapi:export` script and
refreshes the served copy):

```bash
node scripts/sync-openapi.mjs --from-checkout ../catalyst
```

Commit the result. The Scalar viewer (`api/reference`) renders whatever is
committed, and `--check` fails when `public/openapi.json` drifts from
`api/openapi.json`.

## The docs agent

For larger sync work, run the docs agent (`tools/docs-agent/`) in `audit`, `diff`,
`feature`, `validate`, or `api` mode. It maps Catalyst changes to affected pages:

```bash
pnpm docs-agent audit --source-repo ../catalyst --docs-repo .
pnpm docs-agent diff --source-repo ../catalyst --docs-repo . \
  --base origin/main --head HEAD --dry-run
```

`diff` and `feature` write proposed changes into the working tree without
committing; `--dry-run` writes nothing. Details in its README.

## Publish

Merge to `main` → Cloudflare Pages builds and deploys to `docs.catalystctl.com`.
Pull requests get preview deployments. Deployment details: `DEPLOYMENT.md`.

## Related

- [API reference](/api/reference/) — the generated endpoint reference this page regenerates.
- [Catalyst repository](https://github.com/catalystctl/catalyst) — the product source the docs describe.
